title: Second-quarter 2026 output, private demand, prices, and corporate profits move on different scales
source_unit: BEA second-estimate quarterly National Income and Product Accounts and corporate-profits estimates

denominator.unit: aggregate US national-accounts series; quarterly percent changes shown at annual rates

observations.method: BEA seasonally adjusted second estimate; quarterly percent changes are displayed at annual rates.
observations.uncertainty: The second estimate is revised as additional source data arrive; aggregate output and private-demand measures do not identify firms, workers, households, or distribution.
observations.subgroup: Aggregate US economy and private domestic purchasers; no industry, firm-size, worker, or household subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: Private final-sales growth can coexist with unequal household purchasing power, imported input dependence, or weak conditions for particular firms and workers.

denominator.unit: aggregate US price-index series; quarterly changes shown at annual rates

core_pce_price_index.unit: percent annual rate from 2026 Q1; excludes food and energy

observations.method: BEA seasonally adjusted quarterly price-index estimates in the second-estimate release.
observations.uncertainty: Price indexes are aggregate measures and do not reproduce any household's basket; the release is a current vintage subject to revision.
observations.subgroup: Aggregate US domestic purchases and personal-consumption price indexes; no household or income subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: An aggregate price increase can be experienced differently by households depending on housing, energy, health, food, transportation, and substitution options.

corporate_profits_current_production_cha.unit: billions of current US dollars from 2026 Q1

prior_quarter_change.unit: billions of current US dollars from 2025 Q4 to 2026 Q1

observations.method: BEA profits from current production, with inventory valuation and capital consumption adjustments, from the second-estimate release.
observations.uncertainty: Corporate profits are aggregate national-account estimates and do not identify profit distribution, firm market power, tax treatment, reinvestment, wages, employment, or worker control.
observations.subgroup: Aggregate US corporate sector; no industry, firm-size, ownership, worker, or household subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: Profit growth can reflect prices, margins, composition, inventory and capital-consumption adjustments, or sector concentration rather than broad productive or social benefit.

related_sources.claim: BEA July personal income and outlays provide a later household-flow context, with a September 30 annual update scheduled.
BLS August labor-market measures provide a separate worker and establishment context.
New York Fed aggregate household-debt measures provide a separate credit-exposure context.

boundary: This record separates real output, private domestic demand, price indexes, and corporate profits. It does not establish household welfare, worker bargaining power, firm-level market power, AI productivity, political meaning, or geopolitical leverage. Quarterly annual-rate changes, monthly national accounts, labor-market surveys, household surveys, and credit records remain different units.
